name: bogie

attributes.attribute: class of trickster figures of the Scottish Highlands
settles in trees, attics, lofts, and other high places
categories include the brownie, boggart, and nuckelavee

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The bogie is a Scottish mythological figure. It is also called the bogle, bug, or bug-a-boo. It names a class of trickster figures. These beings live in the Scottish Highlands. There March 29 was Bogle Day. Bogies also appear in England. They can move about in troops. Others go alone as solitary fairies. Bogies favor elevated roosts such as trees, attics, and lofts. Many categories of bogie exist. They differ by attire and attitude. They include the helpful brownie. They include the tormenting boggart. They include the destructive nuckelavee. Some goblins appear in a devilish skeletal form.

okr.objective: Describe the bogie as a class of trickster figures spanning several spirit forms.
key_results: The bogie is known as the bogle, bug, or bug-a-boo.
March 29 is Bogle Day in the Scottish Highlands.
Bogies settle in high places and can move in troops or alone.
Its categories include the brownie, the boggart, and the nuckelavee.
